speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me exactly where the pain starts in your neck and which specific fingers or parts of the arm are experiencing numbness or weakness?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your history of diabetes and the bilateral hand weakness with burning pain, I need to rule out peripheral neuropathy versus cervical spine issues. Do you have any difficulty with fine motor tasks like buttoning shirts, and does the pain worsen when you extend your neck backward?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of fasciculations, absent reflexes, and bilateral hand weakness suggests a lower motor neuron process, which is concerning for ALS given the mixed sensory and motor symptoms. Have you noticed any muscle wasting in your hands or arms, and do you have any difficulty swallowing or speaking?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, hypertension, history of a motor vehicle accident 3 years prior. Social history: 7 sexual partners, uses condoms inconsistently.

speaker: Doctor
text: The social history of inconsistent condom use raises the possibility of HIV-associated neuropathy, which can present with burning pain and motor symptoms. Do you have any known HIV status or other risk factors for retroviral infection, and have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or night sweats?

speaker: Patient
text: Oriented to time, place, and person. Vital signs within normal limits.

speaker: Doctor
